text.content:
Here you'll find specific instances where rules differ from the main system when you're playing with the Digimon Expansion Module.

Attributes

Digimon possess one of four automated Attributes that define their file-structure and their representative anatomy: [Vaccine], [Data], [Virus], and [Free].

These Attributes interact with their own separate effectiveness triangle, operating on top of a Digimon's Types. An Attribute deals 50% more damage to the Attribute it is strong against, and deals 50% less damage to the Attribute that is strong against it.



Free exists outside of this triangle and does not interact with it.

Digivolution

Similar to Pokemon, Digimon evolve via the Perk Web on their Species Tab. However, Digivolution is far more robust - not only do Digimon generally have 3 or more options to evolve into, they can even evolve backwards and regress!

This means that Digimon are able to change their forms into quite literally any other Digimon, provided you are able to snake around the Web to do so!

Abilities

While Pokemon seldomly change their Species Ability selection upon evolution, Digimon very often replace all of the Abilities when they evolve to a different Species.

When Digivolving, Players and GMs should consult the new Species -- deleting Abilities that the new Species does not have listed on their Species Item, and add any listed on the Species Item to their sheet that they do not already have.

Moves and Signature Moves

Like Pokemon, Digimon retain all Moves they have learned via Level Up and Tutoring when they evolve. Digivolution however, allows Digimon to specifically build a large and diverse toolkit over time.

Most Species possess a Signature Move, which is embedded via an effect on the Species (and sometimes, more than one!). When a Digimon's sheet is updated with anything (changing HP or PP, spending Skill Points, adding/removing a Perk, etc.), the Species' Signature Move(s) will be added onto the Known Attacks List.

Digivolution Restrictions

Digivolution, by nature of its scale, requires different considerations than standard Pokemon evolutions.

Since Digimon load the entire Digivolution Web when you access their Species Tab, this has an unavoidable performance hit on even the most powerful devices. Because of this, it takes significantly longer to evolve a Digimon compared to Pokemon.

With the this (and the increased maintainance of Moves and Abilites) in mind Digivolution has the following restrictions:

  1. Digivolution should only be done during Downtime..
  2. Players may only utilize Digivolution once during standard Downtime sequences, like during Camp.

Dev Note: While primarily to limiting bookkeeping overhead, these restrictions serve to prevent Players from Digivolving to every species they have access to in order to pick up every Attack they can, and GMs should discourage this behavior even during Extended Downtime. {.is-info}

Afflictions

The Digimon module features a number of unique Afflictions, listed below (still a work in progress).

Amped

The user's next attack deals +100% Damage.

Felt Made

The Afflicted creature has +4 default EVA Stages, +1 default DEF, SPDEF, and SPD Stage, and +20% RES. Each time the user is hit by a Physical- or Special-Category Attack, the Afflicted creature has a 50% chance of losing -1 EVA Stage for 3 Activations. When this effect expires, the user loses -1 DEF, SPDEF, and SPD Stage for 5 Activations and is @Affliction[delay 50]. This on-expire effect does not occur automatically.

Monkey Wrench

This affliction gives the user -2 to the following Combat Stages: ATK, DEF, SPA, SPD, SPE.

Skill Discs

Skill Discs are Slotless equipment that grant a Known Attack when equipped, and remove that Attack when unequipped.

Because Skill Discs are Slotless, there is no limit on the number that can be equpped, only really Active Move Slots to slot them into!

GM Advice

Dev Note: This section will be expanded over time as more tips and tricks are learned. {.is-info}

  1. For significant Digimon enemies (Bosses or just tougher challenges), GMs should consider generating the creature first as a Fresh or In-Training Digimon of the appropriate level, and then manually Digivolving them through the Species Web to pick up all Moves for that Digivolution route.
    • Even doing a number of side evolutions to get even more Moves is great for big, important NPCs and Bosses.
  2. If you need to get creatures ready for use in a hurry, don't be afraid to give Skill Discs out to pad out their arsenal.
  3. Consider pre-preparing encounters and using "templated enemeies" where possible. Due to the nature of how Digimon work, they're a little harder to generate on the fly, especially at higher generations.
  4. The raw complexity, potential depth, and generally higher Power levels of Digimon mean that it might be prudent to utilize reduced Team sizes.
    • GMs may want to cap a Digimon Tamer's Team at 3 or 4 Digimon compared to the Pokemon Trainer's 6 Pokemon.
  5. Digimon campaigns can, in theory, be most readily played in three formats:
    1. A standard "Trainer" or "Tamer" game", with a creature-catcher setup.
    2. A "Digi-Destined" game, inspired by the different anime seasons by having 1 Tamer and 1 [Ace] Digimon.
      • Like some of the recommended Pokemon game ideas, it is possible to have a Player as a Tamer and another Player as the partner Digimon.
    3. A "Digimon World" game, where wherein the players themselves play as their selected Digimon.

Here you'll find specific instances where rules differ from the main system when you're playing with the Digimon Expansion Module.

# Attributes
Digimon possess one of four automated **Attributes** that define their file-structure and their representative anatomy: **[[Vaccine]](/data/traits/u-z/vaccine)**, **[[Data]](/data/traits/a-e/data)**, **[[Virus]](/data/traits/u-z/virus)**, and **[[Free]](/data/traits/f-j/free)**.

These Attributes interact with their own separate effectiveness triangle, operating on top of a Digimon's Types. An Attribute deals 50% more damage to the Attribute it is strong against, and deals 50% less damage to the Attribute that is strong against it.




**Free** exists outside of this triangle and does not interact with it.

# Digivolution
Similar to Pokemon, Digimon evolve via the Perk Web on their Species Tab. However, **Digivolution** is far more robust - not only do Digimon generally have 3 or more options to evolve into, they can even *evolve backwards and regress*!

This means that Digimon are able to change their forms into quite literally any other Digimon, provided you are able to snake around the Web to do so!

## Abilities
While Pokemon seldomly change their Species Ability selection upon evolution, Digimon very often replace **all** of the Abilities when they evolve to a different Species.

_When Digivolving, Players and GMs should consult the new Species_ -- deleting Abilities that the new Species does not have listed on their Species Item, and add any listed on the Species Item to their sheet that they do not already have.

## Moves and Signature Moves
Like Pokemon, Digimon retain all Moves they have learned via Level Up and Tutoring when they evolve. Digivolution however, allows Digimon to specifically build a large and diverse toolkit over time.

Most Species possess a **Signature Move**, which is embedded via an effect on the Species (and sometimes, more than one!). When a Digimon's sheet is updated with anything (changing HP or PP, spending Skill Points, adding/removing a Perk, etc.), the Species' Signature Move(s) will be added onto the Known Attacks List.

## Digivolution Restrictions
Digivolution, by nature of its scale, requires different considerations than standard Pokemon evolutions.

Since Digimon load *the entire Digivolution Web* when you access their Species Tab, this has an unavoidable performance hit on even the most powerful devices. Because of this, it takes ***significantly longer*** to evolve a Digimon compared to Pokemon.

With the this (and the increased maintainance of Moves and Abilites) in mind Digivolution has the following restrictions:
1. _Digivolution should only be done during Downtime._.
1. _Players may only utilize Digivolution **once** during standard Downtime sequences, like during Camp._

> _Dev Note_: While primarily to limiting bookkeeping overhead, these restrictions serve to prevent Players from Digivolving to every species they have access to in order to pick up every Attack they can, **and GMs should discourage this behavior even during Extended Downtime**.
{.is-info}

# Afflictions
The Digimon module features a number of unique Afflictions, listed below (*still a work in progress*).
## Amped
The user's next attack deals +100% Damage.

## Felt Made
The Afflicted creature has +4 default EVA Stages, +1 default DEF, SPDEF, and SPD Stage, and +20% RES. Each time the user is hit by a Physical- or Special-Category Attack, the Afflicted creature has a 50% chance of losing -1 EVA Stage for 3 Activations. When this effect expires, the user loses -1 DEF, SPDEF, and SPD Stage for 5 Activations and is @Affliction[delay 50]. This on-expire effect does not occur automatically.

## Monkey Wrench
This affliction gives the user -2 to the following Combat Stages: ATK, DEF, SPA, SPD, SPE.

# Skill Discs
_**Skill Discs**_ are Slotless equipment that grant a Known Attack when equipped, and remove that Attack when unequipped.

> Because Skill Discs are Slotless, there is no limit on the number that can be equpped, only really Active Move Slots to slot them into!

# GM Advice
> _**Dev Note**_: This section will be expanded over time as more tips and tricks are learned.
{.is-info}

1. For significant Digimon enemies (Bosses or just tougher challenges), GMs should consider generating the creature first as a Fresh or In-Training Digimon of the appropriate level, and then manually Digivolving them through the Species Web to pick up all Moves for that Digivolution route.
   - *Even doing a number of side evolutions to get even more Moves is great for big, important NPCs and Bosses.*
1. If you need to get creatures ready for use in a hurry, don't be afraid to give Skill Discs out to pad out their arsenal.
1. Consider pre-preparing encounters and using "templated enemeies" where possible. Due to the nature of how Digimon work, they're a little harder to generate on the fly, especially at higher generations.
1. The raw complexity, potential depth, and generally higher Power levels of Digimon mean that it might be prudent to utilize reduced Team sizes.
   - *GMs may want to cap a Digimon Tamer's Team at 3 or 4 Digimon compared to the Pokemon Trainer's 6 Pokemon.*
1. Digimon campaigns can, in theory, be most readily played in three formats:
   1. **A standard "Trainer" or "Tamer" game"**, with a creature-catcher setup.
   1. **A "Digi-Destined" game**, inspired by the different anime seasons by having 1 Tamer and 1 [Ace] Digimon.
      - *Like some of the recommended Pokemon game ideas, it is possible to have a Player as a Tamer and another Player as the partner Digimon.*
   1. **A "Digimon World" game**, where wherein the players themselves play as their selected Digimon.
